entry.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
entry.summary:
Indirect prompt-injection (IPI) benchmarks predominantly test planted instructions that redirect a tool-using agent toward an attacker-chosen task. Yet attacker-controlled content can instead tamper with the outcome of the task already in progress. A buyer's dispute evidence can cite a false refund policy to inflate a refund without changing the task.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #agents

entry.title: Generalized Batched Decomposition Key-Switching for CKKS. In lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes, ciphertexts carry an inherent noise that grows as computation advances.
entry.summary:
In lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes, ciphertexts carry an inherent noise that grows as computation advances. The key-switching procedure of these schemes allows the homomorphic re-encryption of a ciphertext under a new secret key, but it incurs substantial noise growth and computational cost. In this work, we generalize the RNS-based decomposition technique of the CKKS scheme to an arbitrary number of input polynomials and secret keys.

entry.title: Atlantis: Lattice-based Anonymous Tokens with Private Metadata Bit. Anonymous tokens with private metadata bit (ATPM) allow an issuer to embed a hidden trust flag, as a single bit, within issued tokens.
entry.summary:
Anonymous tokens with private metadata bit (ATPM) allow an issuer to embed a hidden trust flag, as a single bit, within issued tokens. The bit remains hidden from the clients, but verifiers can read the bit and rate-limit or discard tokens marked suspect. A series of ATPM constructions exist in the literature, however all current constructions rely on classical hardness assumptions such as RSA groups, pairings, or elliptic-curve VRFs and do not provide any post-quantum security guarantees.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #post-quantum

entry.title: Dynark: Making Groth16 Dynamic
entry.summary:
In recent years, numerous new and more efficient constructions of zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge (zkSNARK) have been proposed, motivated by their growing practical applications. However, in most schemes, when the witness is changed, the prover has to recompute the proof from scratch even if the new witness is close to the old one. This is inefficient for applications where proofs are generated for dynamically changing witnesses with small changes.

entry.title: Linear Cryptanalysis with Bibrace Characters: Weak-Key Distinguishers for CRAFT
entry.summary:
Linear cryptanalysis measures the correlation of a cipher with the characters of the group used to define differences. If that group is replaced by a second elementary abelian group structure on the same set, here the one coming from a binary bibrace, then the admissible masks are no longer the ordinary scalar products: exactly half of them survive, and the other half are forced to be quadratic. Beyne's geometric approach develops linear cryptanalysis over an arbitrary finite abelian group, providing a natural framework for this setting.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #clean-tech #computer-vision
